title: Converged Console Hub: rollouts-first workspace matrix and progressive sidebar
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Goal: unify workspace switching, rollout controls, and cost/latency lenses into a single, discoverable hub while preserving quick single-click routes for high-frequency tasks. The proposal replaces disparate workspace jump flows with a workspace matrix inside a compact sidebar expansion. Key pieces: 1) progressive sidebar that expands to show contextual lanes (workspaces, routes, rollout states), 2) workspace matrix modal for multi-tenant role views and pinned workspaces, 3) cost/latency mini-panels attached to each workspace row (hover + pin states), 4) rollout micro-controls (canary toggle, traffic split slider) surfaced inline for routes that support rollouts.

Design rationale: our telemetry shows >40% of console sessions use cross-workspace navigation during deployments and cost-analysis tasks. Users repeatedly switch contexts to check rollout status and cost impact; the aim is to reduce cognitive overhead by exposing rollout state and cost delta inline, and provide a focused matrix for multi-workspace orchestration. We prioritize discoverability and consistency with existing Console metaphors (cards, lanes) while introducing a compact interaction pattern to avoid vertical bloat.

Trade-offs considered: 1) Inline rollout controls reduce clicks but increase surface area in the sidebar; mitigations include progressive reveal and role-aware defaults. 2) Workspace matrix modal centralizes power actions but may be a modal anti-pattern for some flows; we will allow deep-linking and keyboard-first navigation to offset modal friction. 3) Cost mini-panels show approximate delta (30m/24h) to avoid heavy backend queries; precise numbers still available on demand via the metrics panel.

Accessibility & keyboard: full keyboard traversal for the matrix (arrow nav, Enter to open workspace, Space to pin), high-contrast token badges, and ARIA labels for rollout sliders. Performance: prototypes tested on low-power devices; sidebar expansion uses virtualization for long workspace lists.

What we tested in prototype: three states (collapsed, expanded, matrix open) across two personas (platform engineer, product manager). Usability sessions (n=6) revealed faster multi-workspace actions (median time to launch canary down 27%) and fewer accidental route switches. Copy and affordances updated per feedback to clarify traffic split semantics.
notes: Decision: proceed with progressive sidebar + matrix. Implementation to start as opt-in feature flag for 2 weeks of experimentation. Follow-up: telemetry hooks for workspace-switch frequency, rollout toggles, and cost lens impressions. Engineering to provide an API for rollout state and traffic-split mutation (ENG-3010).
